messages:
ana: Running into a bad onboarding experience: the JS quickstart fails on Vercel Edge with "ReferenceError: require is not defined". Users copy-paste and hit runtime error.

ravi: That means our npm package main is CJS. Edge functions need ESM. What's the quickstart import?

ana: Quickstart currently shows `const Redwood = require('redwood-inference')` in the example.

kelly: Oof. Two problems: runtime (ESM vs CJS) and TypeScript types resolution for some bundlers. We need conditional exports and proper types field.

ravi: Proposal: keep dual outputs but make exports map explicit. Example (high level):
`exports.{"import":"./dist/index.mjs","require":"./dist/index.cjs","browser":"./dist/index.browser.mjs","types":"./dist/index.d.ts"}`

kelly: Also add a small worker-target bundle that uses web fetch + AbortController. Our retry layer currently uses node-fetch-specific options which Cloudflare/Workers reject. That causes `Request init contains unsupported member` errors.

taylor: I suggest implementing a small fetch adapter with two builds: fetch.node.ts and fetch.web.ts, compile-time switch so worker build doesn't include node bits. Keeps API the same for retry logic.

ana: For docs: change quickstart to show `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` for modern usage and add a short note for CJS: `const Redwood = require('redwood-inference').default || require('redwood-inference')` so old CommonJS consumers are covered.

ravi: CI: do we run full dual build matrix (cjs+esm+browser) or emit esm + tiny cjs shim? Dual builds increase CI time but reduce surprises for consumers and bundlers. Shim simpler but brittle.

kelly: My vote: dual builds for now. Also add tests: install packed tarball into a Next.js Edge function, Cloudflare Worker, and Node 14 project. Smoke tests should run before release.

taylor: Types nuance: if our main .d.ts references DOM types (RequestInit, AbortSignal), Node-only consumers without `lib: ["DOM"]` will see errors. Two options: emit DOM-agnostic types for main export and ship an extra `worker.d.ts` that augments globals for browser/worker consumers. Document that worker consumers may need `lib: ["DOM","WebWorker"]`.

ana: Good call. Also mention typesVersions if we want to map old TS resolutions. But that adds complexity. Prefer a single d.ts + optional worker augment file.

build-bot: created package canary: `canary/edge-fix` with worker bundle included.

docs-bot: created issue #447: "SDK: conditional exports + worker bundle + typing fixes" assigned to @devex.

ravi: Action items: I'll draft the package.json exports + CI matrix change. Kelly/Taylor will implement fetch adapter and worker build. Ana will update quickstart and add a note about TS lib settings.

kelly: One more runtime note: model-serving code uses setInterval/setTimeout for KV refresh tasks; in worker builds we must ensure timers behave as expected or move to on-demand refresh. Flagging eng-runtime to verify.

taylor: I'll stub a no-op timer shim in worker build if needed and log a warning.

ana: Thanks team. Let's keep the patch limited: add exports map, build fetch adapter, produce worker bundle, update quickstart and types. Ship patch once smoke tests pass. :thumbsup:
